key_insight: Combining a much larger, higher-quality real-world DfD benchmark (ZEDD) with a purpose-built network (FOSSA) enables reliable zero-shot depth estimation from focus stacks across unseen scenes.
problem_solved: Depth-from-defocus models that overfit to specific datasets; the paper addresses the practical challenge of producing dense metric depth maps from focus stacks that generalize zero-shot to new real-world scenes.
method: ZEDD benchmark: introduce a real-world DfD dataset with ~8.3× more scenes and higher-quality images and ground-truth depth than prior benchmarks to evaluate generalization.
FOSSA network: design a novel architecture tailored to process focus stacks and predict dense metric depth with robustness to domain shifts.
Zero-shot evaluation protocol: emphasize cross-dataset testing to measure and drive true out-of-domain performance rather than dataset-specific tuning.
impact: Gives researchers and practitioners a realistic benchmark and a modeling approach focused on cross-domain robustness, reducing the need for dataset-specific retraining and accelerating deployment of depth-from-defocus systems in diverse real-world applications.
visual_elements: Focus-stack → predicted depth: side-by-side panels showing input focus slices, RGB composite, and resulting dense depth map (qualitative example).
Dataset comparison bar chart: ZEDD vs prior benchmarks (number of scenes, image/GT quality) highlighting the 8.3× scale-up.
FOSSA architecture diagram: high-level flow from focus-stack input through fusion/attention modules to metric depth output.
Zero-shot performance plot: scatter or bar chart showing cross-dataset evaluation results (generalization-focused metric).
paper_authors: Yiming Zuo, Hongyu Wen, Venkat Subramanian, Patrick Chen, Karhan Kayan
